clue.text: Leaves a bit depressed alas; Des so tired in retirement

indicators.note: in retirement says the hidden letters are read backwards
a bit says only a small part of the following words is wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone called Des is feeling low and worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Leaves a bit' as the definition, but 'a bit' is what signals the hidden run; 'Leaves' alone defines the dish. Read backwards ('in retirement') from depresseD ALAS DES SO Tired.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of mixed salad greens is literally a bowl of leaves, so leaves stands in for it by example.

clue.text: Following tummy upset, old fellow's thrown up uncooked, tough game

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: the gut is the stomach or tummy
F is the abbreviation for fellow

indicators.note: thrown up in a down clue means the word goes upwards, written in reverse

parts.note: raw means uncooked

explanation.surface: An old man vomiting raw food after a stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' and 'thrown up' read as illness but are two reversal signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Teams heaving on a rope against each other play a contest of brute strength, a hard game.

clue.text: Where to glide over the surface endlessly with plastic poles

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to skim is to move lightly over the surface

indicators.note: plastic means pliable and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A skier gliding on plastic poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' looks like the material of the poles but signals the rearrangement of POLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowy run on a hillside is the place where skiers glide downhill.

clue.text: Moose finally died, poor boy

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word
poor means in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A moose has died, poor thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie is a common male first name, so it is an example of a boy.

clue.text: Observe Labour PM dropping a couple of tabs in the city in Washington

indicators.note: dropping means these letters are taken out

parts.note: to see is to observe
Clement Attlee was the post-war Labour prime minister
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so two tabs are two of that letter

explanation.surface: A British politician taking ecstasy pills in a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' tabs reads as taking drugs. Clement Attlee was the UK's Labour prime minister 1945-51; an E is an ecstasy tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington State, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Bachelor freed from desolate, uncovered cell having loss of fluid

indicators.note: freed from means the letter is let out of the word

parts.note: bleak means desolate

indicators.note: uncovered in a down clue means the top letter is taken off

parts.note: a cage is a cell for confinement

explanation.surface: A bachelor released from a grim prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluid escaping from a container or pipe is a leak, so loss of liquid is its noun.

clue.text: Absolutely hated grid construction

indicators.note: construction means building something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone saying they completely loathe building crossword grids.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone is completely correct is an emphatic way of agreeing absolutely.

clue.text: Went off at first light?

definitions.meaning: to have gone off first, at the head of a group, is to have taken the lead
a light-emitting diode, the small indicator lamp on gadgets

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the past of the verb to lead, going first; the other is the abbreviation for a light-emitting diode.

clue.text: Israeli lithograph featuring Talmudic demon

indicators.note: featuring means the answer appears within the words

explanation.surface: An Israeli print depicting a figure from Jewish lore.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish folklore and the Talmud, Lilith is a female night demon.

clue.text: Gorgeous nymph rejecting a diamond ring, having lost heart

indicators.note: rejecting means turned back, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamond

indicators.note: lost heart means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman turning down an engagement ring and feeling dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamond ring' reads as jewellery but splits into D and a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is the beautiful nymph of Greek myth who turned into a laurel to escape Apollo.

clue.text: Greek Independent for Labour

parts.note: IND is the standard abbreviation for Independent, as on ballot papers

explanation.surface: A Greek independent politician standing for the Labour party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party but is just hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean hard, monotonous toil, so they are synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Amateur reservist lass to run backside off, going lickety-split

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
a gal is a girl or lass

indicators.note: backside off says the rear letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to lope is to run with a long easy stride

explanation.surface: A part-time soldier's girlfriend sprinting away at full pelt.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's volunteer reserve. 'backside off' cuts the last letter from LOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lickety-split is an informal word for very fast, the same as moving at full speed like a horse.

clue.text: She has small parts in Elf, Matrix, Trading Places

indicators.note: the film title is read as letters trading places with each other, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An actress with bit parts in three well-known films.
explanation.walkthrough: The three film titles look like a list of credits, but two are the letters to rearrange and the third, 'Trading Places', is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A background performer in movies has only small walk-on parts, so she is someone with minor roles.

clue.text: Regular helpings of roast loin sell out

indicators.note: regular helpings means every other letter is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone serving equal portions of a pork joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform on or betray someone is to sell them out, an informal phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: OK program to roam when mobile

parts.note: an app is a program, especially one on a mobile phone
to rove is to roam or wander

explanation.surface: Approving a piece of software that lets you wander about with your phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when mobile' just underlines that an app is a mobile program.
explanation.definitionFit: To OK something, as a verb, is to sanction or give it the go-ahead.

clue.text: He repels Pam after rotten time in the middle of nowhere

indicators.note: after says the second group comes after the first

parts.note: off means gone bad or rotten

indicators.note: repels means drives back, so the name is reversed

explanation.surface: A man fending off Pam after an awful time somewhere remote.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere so remote it would not be marked on charts is a long way from anywhere.

clue.text: See 26
See 23
Therapy for uptight Yankee sibling

parts.note: anal, short for anal-retentive, means fussy and uptight
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
sis is short for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: An uptight American's brother or sister seeking therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalysis, a kind of talking therapy, is often called just this, especially in the US.

clue.text: Benitez sent back whence he came?

indicators.note: sent back says the name is written in reverse order

parts.note: Rafa Benitez is the Spanish football manager

explanation.surface: A football manager sacked and returned to where he came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Rafa Benitez is a Spanish football manager who worked in England, hence the question mark on the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: He came to England from a distant country, i.e. from a long way away.

clue.text: Unhealthy allure about British disease

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the next letter is placed inside
unhealthy means unwell, so the letters are in a bad state and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sickly glamour surrounding a British illness.
explanation.definitionFit: German measles is a mild viral infection, an example of a disease.

clue.text: Maybe Gooch, Boycott hosting a TMS broadcast

indicators.note: hosting means the first word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to boycott something is to ban it

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two England cricketers, Graham Gooch and Geoffrey Boycott, appearing on Test Match Special, the BBC radio cricket show.
explanation.walkthrough: Boycott looks like the second cricketer but is just a verb; 'broadcast' rearranges A TMS to ATSM.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Gooch was an England opening bat, an example of a player who bats.

clue.text: Pretentious nonsense! BBC boss taking over symbol of Britishness

parts.note: bull is short for bullshit, pretentious nonsense

indicators.note: taking means holding, so the next letter goes inside

parts.note: the BBC is run by its Director General, DG
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone scoffing at the head of the BBC taking charge of a national emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking over' reads as seizing control, but splits into the insertion signal and O. The BBC's chief executive is its Director General.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulldog, linked with John Bull and Churchill, is a national emblem of Britain.

clue.text: Brand new bunk beds both stripped to accommodate American

indicators.note: to accommodate means to make room inside for the next letters
both stripped means each of the two words loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Stripping new bunk beds to put up a visiting American.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping 'bunk' and 'beds' of their outer letters leaves UN and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never yet used is in mint condition, i.e. brand new.

clue.text: Rehearsal for the Sahara marathon?

definitions.meaning: a practice run-through before the real thing
a long race through the desert would literally be a run in parched conditions

explanation.definitionFit: A practice performance is a trial, and a desert race is literally a run with no water.

clue.text: Martin Crane? Oh…that's upset, like, half a continent

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Martin Crane, the father in the US sitcom Frasier, being dismayed by something.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin Crane, from Seattle, is himself an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being from the northern half of the Americas, the US and Canada, is to be like half a continent.

clue.text: Had dinner with artist, splitting bill two ways

indicators.note: splitting says these letters break the next word apart and sit inside it

parts.note: ate means had a meal
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: Dining with a painter and going halves on the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting bill two ways' reads as sharing the cost but is the insertion signal plus the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral means having two sides or involving two parties, so it works both ways.

clue.text: Trunk's one end of elephant, roughly

indicators.note: one end of picks out the final letter of the word

parts.note: or so means roughly or approximately

explanation.surface: An elephant's trunk is at one end of it, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' points at the elephant but means the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body, without head or limbs, is a synonym for the torso.

clue.text: S. Coe's rival, having given blood, urges a protein boost at breakfast

parts.note: Steve Cram was a British middle-distance rival of Sebastian Coe in the 1980s
bled means having lost or given blood
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: An athlete fuelling up on protein after donating blood.
explanation.walkthrough: Seb Coe and Steve Cram were British middle-distance runners of the 1980s; the initial S plus CRAM gives the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of beaten cooked eggs is a protein-rich morning meal.

clue.text: They did a stretch in prison

definitions.text: They did a stretch in prison

parts.words: They did a stretch in prison
parts.note: doing a stretch means serving a jail term, but here the torture frames literally stretched prisoners

explanation.definitionFit: Medieval torture frames pulled prisoners' limbs, so they stretched people held in jail.

clue.text: Chap's dead leg

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A man who has a numb leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a gentleman, from the Spanish title, and also an Oxbridge fellow; either is a chap.

clue.text: Areas where Sterling's tackling left Gray struggling?

indicators.note: tackling means the first word wraps round the letters it takes on

parts.note: British money, sterling, is counted in pounds

indicators.note: struggling means the name is in disarray, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Football: Raheem Sterling tackling a left-sided player called Gray, who is having a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: Sterling looks like the England footballer but means British money; 'struggling' turns GRAY into AYGR.
explanation.definitionFit: Places set aside for children to play in are kinds of outdoor area.
